registry_entries.name: Produce a unit in the field
registry_entries.summary: For a large price and a long wait, bring a full, lasting unit into play at your side, away from any factory; short-lived escorts are launch-drones.

open_points: produce-unit-in-field stays a validator error until the Vimana's abilities/0 (Summon Caretaker) also links it. Keep launch-drones on that ability too: the six Combat Servitors are short-lived escorts.

The Vimana is not in build-linked-exits' source_units, although the task listed it as a user. Only its combos/1 names the pattern (the Thunderhead teammate that carries Dominance Arcs), and sync-patterns counts only abilities, weapons and modes. No Vimana ability does linked exits, so source_units is the Thunderhead alone.

Removing fit notes shifts the indexes of later notes. The integrator should remove Vimana fit_notes/2, Thunderhead fit_notes/2 and Chinook fit_notes/0 by their content (or in descending order) and then run npm run sync-patterns and npm run docs.

I made the Combat Chinook's fit-note request (clearing an enemy-held building from above) the storm-a-garrison variant of drop-in-from-above, not a new id. The Chinook's capture is a drop onto the building, with the same counterplay: shoot the carrier, bleed the drop. drop-in-from-above.json asks in open_questions whether a separate pattern for clearing a garrison without a drop is wanted later (Generals flash-bangs, microwave tank, bunker busters).
I made the Thunderhead's fit_notes/2 the recall-to-carrier variant of build-linked-exits: the exit is the moving carrier, and if the shelter is destroyed everyone inside dies.
William Mason's Requisition is the call-down-machine variant of drop-in-from-above. His unit record also names transform's shell-and-pilot variant; this is left as an open question in the file.

produce-unit-in-field overlaps with command-companion, which another job of this batch proposes for Anna Kos and Olga Morozova. The suggested line: a companion comes back for free after a wait, while a produced unit is bought again each time. This is recorded in open_questions.

iron-harvest.shared.engineer fit_notes/0 (building production buildings inside the base zone) is not covered by produce-unit-in-field. produce-unit-in-field.json asks whether it should be a variant or a pattern of its own.
The design choices for the player versions are proposals for review, such as an AI-run produced unit that a respawning teammate can claim, a deploy-based host, and drop markers.
